messages.content: What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?

message.content: The lion (Panthera leo) and the zebra (Equus quagga) belong to two very different mammalian orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of all **Laurasiatherian** mammals, which is also the last common ancestor of all placental mammals. This ancestor lived roughly 90–110 million years ago, during the late Cretaceous period, before the diversification of the major placental lineages.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. The lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) are both mammals, but belong to different orders: lions are Carnivora, zebras are Perissodactyla. Their common ancestor would be at the level of the last common ancestor of all placental mammals? Actually, the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals? Wait, let's think: Carnivora and Perissodactyla diverged from each other within Laurasiatheria. The last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla is the last common ancestor of all Laurasiatheria. But the last common ancestor of all placental mammals is older. So the common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which lived around 100 million years ago. But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species: the last common ancestor of the family Felidae and Equidae. That would be the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of all Laurasiatheria. That ancestor would have lived about 90-100 million years ago. So the answer: the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, or more specifically the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatheria clade. So we can say: the last common ancestor of the lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals, which existed around 100 million years ago. Or we can mention the last common ancestor of the two orders: the last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla, which is the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria. So answer accordingly.
